findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and propagate fs::read_to_string errors with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with fewer than 2 fields panics via IndexOutOfBounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') for single-separator parsing, or parts.first()/get() with typed error return

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line missing second field panics via IndexOutOfBounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') for single-separator parsing, or parts.first()/get() with typed error return

findings.failure_mode: any non-u32 value in second column aborts the thread instead of yielding a typed Parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| Error::Parse(e)) and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: as u16 performs lossy truncation on u32 parse result
findings.failure_mode: values outside u16 range silently wrap (e.g. 65536 becomes 0), producing corrupt records with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| Error::OutOfRange) to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds I/O side effect inside data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: core calculation function leaks logging into its return value semantics; cannot be tested deterministically without capturing stdout
findings.fix: move println! to the imperative shell layer; expose a pure parse function that returns data only

findings.problem: load_frames mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested without filesystem setup; I/O errors are lost inside Vec return type
findings.fix: split into pure parse_lines(&[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and shell function load_frames(path) that handles fs I/O and delegates to parse_lines

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failure modes (I/O, parse, bounds, range) are silenced via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish missing file, malformed CSV, invalid number, or out-of-range value
findings.fix: define a domain Error enum (Io, Parse, OutOfRange) and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: collects every split part into Vec<String> before extracting two fields
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; scales poorly with wide CSV lines; wastes memory when only two fields are needed
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') and map the two parts directly, avoiding intermediate Vec<String>

findings.problem: no try_reserve on the output Vec; capacity is unbounded
findings.failure_mode: large input files can trigger allocation failure mid-collection with a panic rather than a typed Allocation error
findings.fix: compute expected capacity from line count or use try_reserve before collecting, mapping alloc-failure to a typed error

findings.failure_mode: performance claims (or lack of regressions) are unmeasured; intermediate Vec<String> per line is a known allocation hotspot
findings.fix: add a benchmark comparing split_once-based parsing vs collect-based parsing with cargo bench; profile with cargo-flamegraph or similar
